subject: Re: Geolocation h - where inference runs & deletion workflow (prospect Q&A)
thread_summary: Prospect asks where LLM requests and derivatives are executed, which subprocessors handle traffic, and how deletion/retention works. Redwood confirms hosted region options (US/EU), provides subprocessor inventory, describes routing and fallback behavior, explains deletion timelines and options for EU-only Dedicated/VPC deployments, and outlines next steps for evidence pack and procurement.
messages:
From: Lina Park <lina.park@acmehealth.com>
To: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Data processing locations and deletion flow — Redwood evaluation

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed I need a concise Q&A for our security review: where do requests to Redwood get processed (regions), which subprocessors see any data, and what the deletion/retention flows look like for both request data and logs? Our legal team is particularly sensitive to any cross-border transfers — Acme Health requires EU-only processing for our EU patient records. Can you confirm what is possible with your hosted offering vs Dedicated/Private?

Appreciate short, concrete answers and any artifacts (subprocessor list, SLA/DPA pointers) you can attach.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Head of Product Security | Acme Health

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data processing locations and deletion flow — Redwood evaluation

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers below (keeping this concise; I attached our subprocessor inventory and a short EU-only guidance sheet):

1) Where inference runs (regions)
- Hosted API (default): We operate region-specific endpoints. For EU requests we offer eu-west (EU) regions and us-west/us-east (US) regions. By default routing is region-aware (client IP + explicit region header) but customers can explicitly pin requests to a region.
- Dedicated / Private: Can be provisioned in a single region (EU-only) — Dedicated pools or a Private VPC package can guarantee that compute and ephemeral caches stay within the selected cloud region(s).

2) Subprocessors who may see data
- For hosted EU processing: compute/storage typically runs on GCP europe-west1 (primary) and may use partner edge/CDN providers for static assets. Our attached inventory lists all subprocessors and their processing role.
- For Hosted US: AWS us-west-2 / GCP us-central are common.
- Note: subprocessor involvement depends on deployment selection (hosted vs Dedicated/Private) and selected add-ons (e.g., CDN, logging retention).

3) Cross-border transfers
- Default hosted routing will keep EU-labeled requests in EU regions where possible. In rare capacity-fallback cases we may route to a nearby, compatible region; such fallback is disabled for customers that require strict EU-only processing (see Private/Dedicated options).

4) Retention & deletion
- Ephemeral inference state (KV cache, in-memory tensors): cleared immediately after request lifecycle; not persisted to durable stores.
- Request payloads and response text: default retention for troubleshooting/analytics is 30 days in hosted plans; customers can request shorter retention windows or opt-out of retention.
- Operational logs/metrics: retained 90 days by default (can be shortened under contract).
- Permanent deletion requests: we provide a documented erase API and support bulk erase workflows; artifacts are removed from primary stores and kicked to deletion pipelines — typical completion within 30 calendar days, full scrub from backups within 90 days unless otherwise contracted.

5) Evidence and next steps
- Attached: redwood_subprocessor_inventory_20280803.pdf (full inventory) and eu-only-processing-guide_2028.xlsx (checklist for EU-only Dedicated).
- If Acme requires a contractual EU-only guarantee we recommend Dedicated (EU region) or Private VPC deployment; I can introduce our deployment team and share a project timeline (typically 4-6 weeks for Dedicated capacity + onboarding).

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call with Vivek (cc’ed) to walk through the evidence pack and confirm any technical constraints.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@acmehealth.com>, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 4 Aug 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data processing locations and deletion flow — Redwood evaluation

Hi Lina — quick technical clarifications to Monica's note:

- Routing & fallbacks: Our smart router evaluates request region preference, capacity, and cost policy. For customers who do not allow cross-border movement we turn off remote fallback and enforce region pinning at the ingress/load-balancer layer (no egress to other compute regions).

- Subprocessor roles: the attached inventory classifies subprocessors as "compute", "storage/backup", "monitoring/telemetry" and "cdn/edge". For EU-only customers we remove non-EU storage and use EU-only monitoring endpoints where available.

- Caching & persistence: KV cache used for inference acceleration is in-process or attached to regional cache clusters; it is not replicated to other regions for EU-only deployments. Model artifacts are stored in regional object storage; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-provided model storage (S3/GCS) to avoid cross-account transfers.

- Deletion mechanics: delete requests trigger a three-stage pipeline (mark-for-delete -> purge primary storage -> scrub backups). We provide timestamped deletion receipts for compliance evidence and can add S3 object lifecycle rules for customer-managed buckets if you choose Private.

Happy to run through the inventory line-by-line on a call if helpful.

— Vivek
Director, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Lina Park <lina.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: acme-security@acmehealth.com

Thanks Monica/Vivek — this is exactly what we needed. Two quick follow-ups: 1) can you mark the subprocessor inventory lines that are used for EU-only Hosted vs those only used for US; and 2) can you share a sample DPA clause for EU-only processing and a rough quote / timeline for EU Dedicated?

If you can also send a DocuSign link for the standard DPA + NDA we can get legal moving.

Lina

On a side note — we’ll plan the technical call early next week; does Monday or Tuesday work for you?
